metrics.name: Connected area ratio
metrics.definition: `A_connected / A_required`, using the connected terrain component serving the layout
metrics.fieldwork: Verify unresolved obstacles and boundaries; ground suitability remains separate

metrics.name: Complete layout fit
metrics.definition: Share of required footprint and clearance polygons fully accommodated, %
metrics.baseline: D: 100%; no overlap with incompatible uses or exclusion zones
metrics.ideal: 100%, plus the specified expansion layout also fits
metrics.fieldwork: Check small obstacles and critical clearances

metrics.name: Required spatial connections
metrics.definition: Required building/equipment/service-zone connections accommodated by valid corridors, %
metrics.ideal: 100%, with a separate alternate corridor to each designated critical zone
metrics.fieldwork: Confirm narrow passages, surface conditions, and access

metrics.name: Overall building-pad slope
metrics.definition: Inclination of fitted pad plane, degrees
metrics.fieldwork: Refine elevations if uncertainty could change acceptance

metrics.name: Maximum local pad slope
metrics.definition: Maximum valid 10 m-window plane slope, degrees
metrics.baseline: P: ≤ 10°; all unresolved/invalid windows remain flagged
metrics.fieldwork: Resolve steep transitions or features smaller than the model

metrics.name: Maximum grading or support correction
metrics.definition: Largest required vertical adjustment from measured ground to the proposed design surface, m
metrics.fieldwork: Detailed elevations at actual support locations

metrics.name: Earthmoving demand
metrics.definition: Cut and fill volumes reported separately, m³; each divided by its equipment/logistics budget
metrics.baseline: D: Each ratio ≤ 1.0, with a feasible material-source/disposal plan
metrics.fieldwork: Identify material properties, excavability, and whether spoil is reusable

metrics.name: Detrended roughness
metrics.definition: Maximum window RMS residual height across the zone, m
metrics.fieldwork: Measure finer surface irregularities

metrics.name: Support-interface variation
metrics.definition: Maximum peak-to-valley height over each actual support/contact footprint, m
metrics.fieldwork: Close-range survey of contact surfaces

metrics.name: Abrupt step height
metrics.definition: Largest measured step on a required vehicle path, m
metrics.fieldwork: Measure vehicle-scale steps and depressions

metrics.name: Unresolved blocking obstacles
metrics.definition: Count intersecting required footprint/clearance polygons with neither avoidance nor a feasible removal plan
metrics.baseline: D: 0 before a screened pass; uncertain removability remains unresolved
metrics.ideal: 0 blockers and no obstacle-removal work required
metrics.fieldwork: Check dimensions, embedded depth, and removability

metrics.name: Obstacle removal demand
metrics.definition: Estimated removal effort divided by the defined removal budget, with machine-hour and mass estimates retained
metrics.baseline: D: ≤ 1.0 and each operation within equipment capability
metrics.fieldwork: Test material, embedded depth, lifting/excavation difficulty

metrics.name: Residual clearance margin
metrics.definition: Minimum distance between obstacle envelope and required operating envelope, including positional uncertainty, m
metrics.baseline: D: ≥ 0; required operational clearances are already included in the envelope
metrics.fieldwork: Verify tight clearances and hidden features

metrics.name: Hazard-envelope overlap
metrics.definition: Required footprint/corridor area intersecting assessed exclusion envelopes, m²
metrics.baseline: D: 0; missing hazard envelopes make the result unresolved
metrics.fieldwork: Investigate unstable material, fractures, and local conditions

metrics.name: Setback adequacy
metrics.definition: Actual distance from relevant hazard source divided by assessed minimum setback `S_required`
metrics.ideal: D/P: ≥ 1.5, where additional separation is practical
metrics.fieldwork: Supply material and stability evidence for hazard analysis

metrics.name: Mobile-terrain clearance
metrics.definition: Distance to moving-material front minus estimated upper-bound encroachment over `T` and uncertainty buffer, m
metrics.fieldwork: Monitor changes and constrain future encroachment

metrics.name: Corridor width
metrics.definition: Minimum usable width along route, m
metrics.baseline: D: ≥ `W + 2C` on straight sections; turns pass swept-envelope checks
metrics.ideal: D/P: ≥ `W + 4C`; turns retain the same additional clearance margin
metrics.fieldwork: Check small obstructions and usable ground

metrics.name: Grade and cross-slope utilization
metrics.definition: Maximum measured longitudinal/cross slopes divided separately by respective validated vehicle limits
metrics.fieldwork: Validate difficult segments and actual mobility conditions

metrics.name: Turning fit
metrics.definition: Share of required maneuvers fitting the validated swept envelope including clearance, %
metrics.fieldwork: Verify tight turns and ground conditions

metrics.name: Route redundancy
metrics.definition: Number of assessed routes between designated delivery/base point and facility without a shared critical chokepoint
metrics.fieldwork: Verify that alternatives are actually traversable

metrics.name: Utility route utilization
metrics.definition: Proposed cable/pipe length divided by design allowance, evaluated for each service
metrics.baseline: D: ≤ 1.0; bend, elevation, loss, and maintenance constraints also pass
metrics.ideal: D/P: ≤ 0.8 with all other constraints passing
metrics.fieldwork: Verify trench conditions, obstacles, and installation details

metrics.name: Bearing-capacity adequacy
metrics.definition: Minimum allowable bearing stress divided by applied design contact stress, dimensionless
metrics.baseline: D: ≥ 1.0 for every support and applicable case
metrics.ideal: D/P: ≥ 1.25 using the same design method
metrics.fieldwork: Soil/rock characterization and appropriate probing/load tests

metrics.name: Other support-limit utilization
metrics.definition: Maximum demand/allowable capacity across applicable anchor, sliding, uplift, and lateral cases
metrics.fieldwork: Material and anchor tests supporting engineering calculations

metrics.name: Total settlement utilization
metrics.definition: Upper-bound predicted settlement divided by design allowance, at each support
metrics.fieldwork: Layering, compressibility, load response, and monitoring

metrics.name: Differential movement utilization
metrics.definition: Maximum relative support movement or angular distortion divided by its respective allowance
metrics.fieldwork: Spatial variability across the footprint

metrics.name: Unresolved ice interactions
metrics.definition: Count of critical supports/corridors whose influence volume intersects possible ice without an evaluated response or mitigation
metrics.ideal: P: 0 and no ice-related mitigation needed beneath critical infrastructure
metrics.fieldwork: Confirm local ice and evaluate disturbance/heating effects

metrics.name: Investigated depth coverage
metrics.definition: Adequately characterized depth divided by required investigation depth, at each designated critical zone
metrics.baseline: D: ≥ 1.0; required horizontal coverage also satisfied
metrics.fieldwork: Depth profiles, radar where suitable, probes or cores

metrics.name: Thermally induced deformation utilization
metrics.definition: Upper-bound predicted displacement from thermal/ice changes divided by its design allowance
metrics.baseline: D: ≤ 1.0 in all required construction and operating cases
metrics.fieldwork: Temperature profiles, ice/material properties, displacement monitoring

metrics.name: Unassessed influence overlap
metrics.definition: Critical foundation/utility area overlapping an unassessed ground-change envelope, m²
metrics.fieldwork: Refine the extent and response of affected ground

metrics.name: Construction-budget utilization
metrics.definition: Required excavation energy, machine-hours and handling mass divided separately by their budgets
metrics.baseline: D: Every ratio ≤ 1.0 and all operations within equipment capability
metrics.fieldwork: Excavation trials and material testing

metrics.name: Unresolved excavation stability cases
metrics.definition: Count of proposed excavations without an assessed stable/supportable configuration
metrics.ideal: P: 0 without special ground treatment beyond standard scenario equipment
metrics.fieldwork: Ground investigation needed to resolve them

metrics.name: Critical-zone evidence completion
metrics.definition: Share of required foundation/corridor zones with the specified spatial/depth characterization, %
metrics.ideal: 100%, plus corroboration for each decision-critical indirect inference
metrics.fieldwork: Complete the missing characterization

metrics.name: Decision-critical unresolved hypotheses
metrics.definition: Count of plausible material/ice interpretations that could reverse acceptance and have not been resolved or bounded
metrics.baseline: D: 0 for acceptance; otherwise an investigation candidate
metrics.ideal: 0, with site ordering unchanged across justified parameter ranges
metrics.fieldwork: Targeted measurements to distinguish competing interpretations

metrics.name: Stop-to-decision traceability
metrics.definition: Stops with a named hypothesis, method, required precision and decision consequence / planned stops, %
metrics.ideal: 100%, with redundant stops removed unless scientifically justified
metrics.fieldwork: Record whether the planned measurement succeeded

metrics.name: Mandatory objective coverage
metrics.definition: Mandatory measurement objectives achievable in this excursion / declared mandatory objectives, %
metrics.baseline: D: 100%, or revise scope before acceptance
metrics.ideal: 100% plus highest-value optional objectives without using mandatory reserves
metrics.fieldwork: Actual task completion and instrument performance

metrics.name: Mobility-limit utilization
metrics.definition: Maximum demand/limit across each relevant grade, cross-slope, step, clearance or ground parameter; formulate ratios so ≤ 1 is acceptable
metrics.baseline: D: Every applicable ratio ≤ 1.0 on outward and return paths
metrics.ideal: D/P: Each ≤ 0.7 where meaningful; otherwise use a design-defined margin
metrics.fieldwork: Local reconnaissance and mobility verification

metrics.name: Assessed route coverage
metrics.definition: Route length with sufficient evidence for all critical mobility checks / total required route length, %
metrics.baseline: D: 100% for a scenario-feasible crewed route
metrics.fieldwork: Reconnaissance of unverified segments

metrics.name: Planned-time utilization
metrics.definition: Upper planning estimate of travel + tasks + return divided by available duration after required contingency reserve
metrics.fieldwork: Actual travel/task timing to refine the model

metrics.name: Return-time feasibility
metrics.definition: Worst-case assessed return time / remaining allowed time after required return contingency, evaluated along route
metrics.baseline: D: ≤ 1.0 at every evaluated state; intervening changes bounded
metrics.fieldwork: Updated location, progress, and route conditions during the mission

metrics.name: Resource utilization
metrics.definition: Required quantity / usable quantity after prescribed reserve, separately for every limiting consumable
metrics.baseline: D: All ≤ 1.0 including return and required contingency cases
metrics.fieldwork: Mission telemetry and activity-specific validation

metrics.name: Return-resource feasibility
metrics.definition: Required quantity to terminate work and return / available remaining quantity after prescribed reserve, per resource along route
metrics.baseline: D: All ≤ 1.0 at every evaluated state
metrics.fieldwork: Actual remaining supplies and current conditions

metrics.name: Instrument and payload readiness
metrics.definition: Mandatory tasks with deployable equipment meeting precision/depth/range, mass, volume, power and data constraints, %
metrics.ideal: 100% plus the specified backup method for decision-critical tasks
metrics.fieldwork: Deployment trials and verification in actual conditions

metrics.name: Longest unsupported communication interval
metrics.definition: Maximum interval without mission-required local communication, minutes
metrics.baseline: D: ≤ mission allowance, with assessed recovery procedure
metrics.ideal: P: 0 where continuous local coverage is practicable
metrics.fieldwork: Local link tests; terrain visibility alone does not prove connectivity

metrics.name: Navigation-error utilization
metrics.definition: Position-error bound / allowable error for the local obstacle corridor or measurement task
metrics.fieldwork: Landmark surveys and localization trials

metrics.name: Environmental-limit utilization
metrics.definition: Exposure or environmental demand / respective allowance, evaluated separately; report temperature limits as margins where ratios are inappropriate
metrics.baseline: D: All limits met with uncertainty accounted for
metrics.ideal: D: All limits plus mission-defined extra margins met
metrics.fieldwork: Local monitoring and mission-time updates

metrics.name: Required contingency coverage
metrics.definition: Defined disruption cases with assessed return/shelter/support response meeting limits, %
metrics.fieldwork: Verify shelter, rescue, vehicle, and route assumptions

metrics.name: Independent return options
metrics.definition: Assessed return options without shared critical failure, available from each designated critical stop
metrics.fieldwork: Verify their traversability and support arrangements

metrics.name: Terrain-shading energy loss
metrics.definition: Difference between unobstructed and terrain-obstructed modeled PV energy divided by unobstructed energy, %; other inputs identical
metrics.baseline: P: ≤ 10% over reference year; seasonal results also reported
metrics.fieldwork: Verify local horizon and shadow timing where uncertain

metrics.name: Row-shading energy loss
metrics.definition: Incremental modeled energy loss from actual array rows, %; ordering of loss attribution stated
metrics.fieldwork: Installation verification; no astronaut measurement inherently required

metrics.name: Average solar contribution
metrics.definition: Net PV energy / elapsed hours of the complete reference period, kW
metrics.baseline: P: ≥ 100 kW for the reference solar option
metrics.ideal: P: ≥ 120 kW within the same installed design and land allowance
metrics.fieldwork: Calibrate with irradiance, panel temperature, dust, and electrical measurements

metrics.name: Worst-season energy adequacy
metrics.definition: Minimum delivered PV energy / specified solar-energy requirement across defined seasonal bins
metrics.baseline: D: ≥ 1.0 in every bin with a nonzero requirement
metrics.fieldwork: Validate seasonal conditions; one visit is insufficient

metrics.name: Soiling-loss allowance utilization
metrics.definition: Worst modeled deposited-dust energy loss between cleanings / allocated soiling loss
metrics.fieldwork: Paired cleaned/soiled panel monitoring at the site

metrics.name: Cleaning-resource utilization
metrics.definition: Cleaning energy, crew/robot hours and consumables divided separately by their budgets
metrics.baseline: D: Every ratio ≤ 1.0 and access feasible
metrics.fieldwork: Representative cleaning trials and access checks

metrics.name: Unserved essential energy
metrics.definition: Integral of unmet essential facility power, kWh, plus outage duration
metrics.ideal: 0 including the agreed additional single-failure stress cases
metrics.fieldwork: Improve environmental inputs; this is not itself a field measurement

metrics.name: Storage-limit violations
metrics.definition: Count of time steps outside energy, charge/discharge power, temperature or reserve limits
metrics.baseline: D: 0; repeat-period model must not borrow unreplenished initial energy
metrics.ideal: 0 with the specified extra storage reserve preserved
metrics.fieldwork: Environmental and system tests for validation

metrics.name: Flexible-work completion
metrics.definition: Delivered compute work by deadline / required scheduled compute work
metrics.ideal: D/P: ≥ 1.1 capability at the same power constraints
metrics.fieldwork: No terrain measurement directly establishes this; hardware/workload tests are central

metrics.name: Array layout accommodation
metrics.definition: Required panel/support/clearance layout accommodated, %
metrics.baseline: D: 100% within permitted terrain and ground zones
metrics.fieldwork: Verify support ground, obstacles, and maintenance access

metrics.name: Electrical-route loss
metrics.definition: Cable/conversion loss assigned to site connections / defined delivered-energy boundary, %
metrics.fieldwork: Installation and performance verification later

metrics.name: Required scenario coverage
metrics.definition: Required seasons, dust cases and operating cases evaluated, %
metrics.fieldwork: Measurements may fill evidence gaps, but the metric is an audit

metrics.name: Validation-error utilization
metrics.definition: Prediction error / defined validation tolerance, with bias and time-profile errors evaluated separately
metrics.fieldwork: Local test-panel and irradiance observations

metrics.name: Environmental case coverage
metrics.definition: Required thermal cases with a bounded, time-dependent environmental input set, %
metrics.ideal: 100%, with independent observations spanning key modeled regimes
metrics.fieldwork: Fill local air, ground-depth, seasonal, and extreme-condition gaps

metrics.name: Enclosure external-envelope margin
metrics.definition: Minimum distance of predicted external conditions from the qualified enclosure/environmental-control envelope, in the applicable units
metrics.fieldwork: Validate local conditions; enclosure qualification also requires engineering tests

metrics.name: Heat-rejection adequacy
metrics.definition: Lower-bound available net rejection / required heat load for each loop and case
metrics.ideal: D/P: ≥ 1.2 without exceeding the same limits
metrics.fieldwork: Instrumented heat-rejection tests to validate local performance

metrics.name: Operating-temperature margin
metrics.definition: Minimum of upper allowable minus predicted upper-bound temperature and predicted lower-bound minus lower allowable, °C or K difference
metrics.baseline: D: ≥ 0 for each applicable component and operating case
metrics.fieldwork: Validate environmental inputs and system behavior

metrics.name: Cold-protection resource utilization
metrics.definition: Required heater power and energy divided separately by available allocations in each survival/startup case
metrics.baseline: D: Both ≤ 1.0 while all survival limits hold
metrics.fieldwork: Cold-condition monitoring and representative system tests

metrics.name: Thermal-cycle utilization
metrics.definition: Maximum ramp rate, temperature excursion and life-cycle count divided separately by qualified limits
metrics.fieldwork: Local monitoring; laboratory/component qualification remains necessary

metrics.name: Adverse-environment rejection penalty
metrics.definition: Modeled reduction in net rejection relative to specified reference exposure divided by allocated penalty
metrics.fieldwork: Measure dust/optical changes and validate thermal performance

metrics.name: Thermal-layout accommodation
metrics.definition: Required radiator/support/clearance/maintenance layout accommodated without violating modeled thermal constraints, %
metrics.ideal: 100% plus the specified modular expansion layout
metrics.fieldwork: Verify ground, nearby surfaces, and critical environmental assumptions

metrics.name: Connection-resource utilization
metrics.definition: Required pump power, pressure head and unwanted thermal exchange divided separately by design budgets
metrics.baseline: D: All applicable ratios ≤ 1.0 with adequate flow and fluid margins
metrics.fieldwork: Route/environment verification and engineering tests

metrics.name: Ground-interaction utilization
metrics.definition: Predicted thermally induced ground displacement / applicable foundation or utility allowance
metrics.baseline: D: ≤ 1.0; unresolved ice interactions prevent a pass
metrics.fieldwork: Subsurface properties, temperature profiles, ice evidence and movement

metrics.name: Required monitoring completion
metrics.definition: Required spatial/time/depth cases supported at specified precision by observations or accepted bounded models, %
metrics.baseline: D: 100% for acceptance; measured and modeled shares shown separately
metrics.ideal: 100%, with local observations for every decision-critical regime
metrics.fieldwork: Install sensors and complete missing observations

metrics.name: Model validation utilization
metrics.definition: Temperature and heat-rejection prediction errors divided by their respective tolerances
metrics.fieldwork: Independent local measurements and equipment tests
